Synopsis:
    The Anglo American / Teck Resources $54bn merger remains pending Chinese regulatory approval one year after announcement, with Beijing having suspended its review clock. Copper hit a record above $14,700/t driven by tight supply, EV/grid demand and US tariff expectations. China has a history of extracting concessions from mining deals (e.g. Glencore/Xstrata). The article also flags EU scrutiny of MMG's purchase of Anglo's Brazilian nickel assets. The broader takeaway: as governments increasingly prioritise supply chain resilience and national security, mining megadeals are becoming slower and costlier to execute.

Risk score: 30 — Chinese regulatory delays in mining M&A are a well-established pattern. The suspended review clock adds some incremental uncertainty, but the broader dynamic is largely known to the market (Teck trades only 1.3% below implied deal value).
